entries.title: The Barrens
body: A vast, sun-scorched savanna in the heart of Kalimdor, ringed by low mountains, one of the largest lands in the world. It was not always barren. Long ago it was forest, tended by the night elves; Queen Azshara's expeditions built outposts in its wilds, and it is said the demigod Lo'Gosh faced the Burning Legion there in the War of the Ancients. War, the Legion and the Great Sundering turned the woodland into the dry plain it is today.

Life clings on around a few oases in the north, fed by waters rising from the Wailing Caverns, whose springs invigorate the plants and beasts that drink them. For generations the tauren roamed the plains hunting kodo and thunder lizards, until the Horde came and made the Barrens the heart of its territory. Now orcish farms, watch towers and caravans dot the land, contested by quilboar, centaurs, harpies, goblins, dwarves and the Alliance.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Barrens (introduction, History, World of Warcraft)

entries.title: The Crossroads
body: The largest Horde town in the northern Barrens, where the Gold Road from the north meets the road running from Ratchet on the coast to the Stonetalon Mountains in the west. Its wind riders fly to nearly every Horde outpost in Kalimdor.

It has few lodgings but is a bustling trade centre, full of traders shouting their wares, and the first place outside the capitals where travellers of the Horde gather in numbers. Just outside the walls is a burial ground where the Horde pays its respects to the dead.

entries.title: Far Watch Post
body: A small Horde outpost just west of the bridge between Durotar and the Barrens: a watch tower, an orc burrow and a few catapults. It is not a welcoming spot, but it is vital for protecting the supply caravans and keeping Durotar safe from the Alliance and the quilboar.

entries.title: Dreadmist Peak
body: A mountain north-west of the Crossroads. Climbing it, the air turns red and foggy: the orange miasma is the residue of an ancient demonic curse. Burning Blade cultists live at the top, guarding the Demon Seed in Dreadmist Den.

Three years after the Third War, the demon Zmodlor, who pulled the strings of the Burning Blade and tried to start a war between the Horde and Theramore, was confronted here by Jaina Proudmoore and the ancient Guardian Aegwynn, and banished into the Twisting Nether.

entries.title: The Forgotten Pools
body: The northernmost of the Barrens' oases, off the western road from the Crossroads. Kolkar centaurs patrol its banks among the turtles, and mushrooms found nowhere else grow along its shore.

entries.title: The Stagnant Oasis
body: An oasis between the Merchant Coast and the Gold Road, with Kolkar centaurs camped on its fringes. Lost kodo wander here, weak and alone and far from their herds.

entries.title: Lushwater Oasis
body: One of the three great oases of the northern Barrens, just south of the Crossroads. Kolkar centaurs stalk between its trees, hunting the beasts that come to drink. On its northern side lies the entrance to the Wailing Caverns.

entries.title: The Wailing Caverns
body: A network of caverns beneath the Barrens whose underground rivers run for miles and bubble up as the land's oases. The night elf druid Naralex discovered them and named them for the mournful howls of the wind and steam moving through their cracks.

Naralex believed that by joining these waters to the Emerald Dream he could make the Barrens green again. He went into the caverns with his disciples and sank into meditation, letting the Dream flow through him into Azeroth. Instead, the Emerald Nightmare overwhelmed him. Unable to wake, he channels its energies into the caverns, corrupting the waters, twisting the beasts into deviate forms, and driving most of his disciples mad. They call themselves the Druids of the Fang.

entries.title: Ratchet
body: A goblin port on the Barrens coast, halfway between Orgrimmar and Theramore, doing most of its business with Booty Bay across the sea. Thrall paid Gazlowe well for his help building Orgrimmar, and with the money Gazlowe founded Ratchet.

It was started by smugglers and filled with their kind, and with everyone else various societies had cast out. Orcs and humans both trade here under the watch of the goblin bruisers, and when the Burning Blade stirred up trouble between Durotar and Theramore, the docks of Ratchet were where tempers flared first.

entries.title: The Merchant Coast
body: The Barrens' short stretch of coastline, named for the lucrative trade that passes through Ratchet's thrifty goblin hands. Fray Island lies offshore, once a training ground for warriors of every race. The southern part of the coast is held by the Southsea Freebooters, pirates who prey on that trade.

entries.title: Northwatch Hold
body: A massive Alliance fortress on a mountain between the Merchant Coast and Dustwallow Marsh, built after the Battle of Mount Hyjal by the human survivors of the expedition to Kalimdor. It blocks the coastal approach to Theramore, and it has its own scrying stone to speak with Jaina's city.

Standing in what was then neutral ground, it has always been a source of distrust between orcs and humans. When it grew, the orc Burx led an army against it without leave, and Thrall stopped the battle himself, learned that Burx served the Burning Blade, and killed him with the Doomhammer.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Northwatch Hold (introduction, Invasion of Durotar)

entries.title: Camp Taurajo
body: A tauren outpost in the southern Barrens near the pass into Mulgore, the largest Horde settlement in the south. It watches the road and the plains, where the tauren once lived as nomads before they had a homeland.

entries.title: Bael Modan
body: A dwarven fortress and excavation in the southern Barrens, with a great cannon on its walls. Beneath it lies an ancient titan complex, and the dwarves of Ironforge under General Twinbraid dig for the relics and knowledge it holds.

Before they came, the land belonged to the Stonespire tauren. The dwarves blasted holy ground with their explosives, and in the conflict that followed most of the Stonespire were killed or driven out. Their village is now torn apart by digging machines. Gann Stonespire tried to make peace with the dwarves, failed, and now seeks revenge.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Bael Modan (introduction, World of Warcraft)

entries.title: The Sludge Fen and Boulder Lode Mine
body: Venture Company holdings in the north-east of the Barrens. The Sludge Fen was once a pool of crystal-blue water; the goblins built an oil rig on it and turned it into a mire of industrial waste. Nearby, Boulder Lode Mine still bears orcish banners from when it belonged to the Horde, before the Venture Company took it.
Ratchet's own goblins of the Tinkers' Union eye the Company's new shredders with envy, and have tried to steal one.

entries.title: Field of Giants
body: The plains of the far southern Barrens between Camp Taurajo and Dustwallow, where herds of thunder lizards, kodo and other great beasts roam. The watch towers along this stretch of the Gold Road have been abandoned.
The great concern of the region is the appearance of silithid hives, the northernmost in all Kalimdor. No one knows yet why the insects have come so far north.

entries.title: The Dry Hills
body: The foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains in the far north-west, which despite their name are one of the greener parts of the Barrens. Witchwing harpies nest there and raid the caravans on the northern Gold Road.

entries.title: Raptor Grounds
body: A small valley in the southern Barrens west of Northwatch Hold, home of the Sunscale raptors. They are odd among their kind, unnaturally intelligent, building crude huts and tools, and drawn to anything shiny, which they steal from the Horde's camps.

entries.title: The Razorfens
body: At the far southern edge of the Barrens rise the great thorn-mounds of the quilboar. Razorfen Kraul, their ancestral home, grew from the thorns said to have sprung from the corpse of the demigod Agamaggan; the crone Charlga Razorflank rules it now. Razorfen Downs, nearby, is the burial ground and traditional capital of their race.
Since the Third War, agents of the Scourge led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer have taken the Downs, and whispers say Charlga has been bargaining with them.

entries.title: The Mor'shan Rampart
body: A defensive post at the northern end of the Gold Road, built to hold back the Alliance pushing south out of Ashenvale. Its watch towers serve as a launching point for raids on the night elf town of Astranaar, and the nearby base camp is home to the Warsong Outriders.

entries.title: Honor's Stand
body: An orcish outpost of burrows and watch towers guarding the western road between the Crossroads and the Stonetalon Mountains. It has seen many great battles in its short life, and the orcs stationed there, even the peons repairing its walls, are proud of its history. The Kolkar centaurs harry it constantly.

entries.title: The Great Lift
body: An elevator built by the tauren to carry travellers between the southern Barrens and the canyons of Thousand Needles far below. The quilboar of the south have spread across the path to it, and the tauren who kept it are not always safe.

entries.title: Gazlowe
body: The goblin baron of Ratchet. He and his workers helped Thrall build Orgrimmar and were paid handsomely for it, and Gazlowe put the money into his own port. He keeps Ratchet neutral and profitable, and dislikes anything, pirates especially, that gets in the way of trade.

entries.title: Gann Stonespire
body: One of the last of the Stonespire tauren, whose village stood beside Bael Modan before the dwarves came. He tried to settle the quarrel over the holy ground peacefully and failed. Now he wanders the roads near the keep, mourning his tribe and seeking revenge.

entries.title: Tonga Runetotem
body: A tauren druid of the Cenarion Circle. With Hamuul Runetotem, he sensed the power of the Wailing Caverns leaking up into the oases, and discovered that it had been tainted, and that the night elf druids who went down into the caverns had been twisted by the Emerald Nightmare.

entries.title: Regthar Deathgate
body: An orc commander who wages the Horde's war against the Kolkar centaurs of the Barrens, the same raiders who hunted the tauren for generations.

entries.title: Mankrik
body: An orc warrior of the Crossroads whose wife, Olgra, went out into the Barrens and never came back. He asks everyone he meets to look for her.

entries.title: Mangletooth
body: A quilboar exile held at Camp Taurajo, who trades the blessings of Agamaggan for the blood shards the Bristleback warriors carry. He is no friend of the leaders of his own people.

entries.title: The Living Oases
body: The oases of the Barrens are fed by the underground rivers of the Wailing Caverns, and their waters carry a life energy that invigorates everything that drinks them. Even the herbs of the Barrens grow slightly differently, changed by the oasis water.
Naralex's dream of a green Barrens made them grow; the Nightmare that took him is making them sick. New oases have sprung up, and so have deviate creatures and corrupted druids.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Barrens (introduction, World of Warcraft, Geography)

entries.title: Agamaggan, the Boar God
body: Ten thousand years ago, in the War of the Ancients, the demigod Agamaggan, a colossal boar, came forth to fight the Burning Legion. He fell in battle, but helped save the world. Where his blood soaked the earth, great thorny vines sprouted.

The quilboar, who believe they are his mortal children, settled in those places and hold them sacred. The heart of each thorn colony is called a Razorfen. The tribes are spiritual, and their greatest warriors are said to carry Agamaggan's strength; they war with each other as readily as with the Horde.

entries.title: The Horde Crosses the Barrens
body: When Thrall's orcs and the Darkspear trolls landed in Kalimdor in the Third War, they marched across the Barrens. Grom Hellscream's Warsong clan crossed it first. Thrall gathered his scattered warriors on the shore, came to the aid of the Bloodhoof tauren, and escorted them across the plains, past the oases, to Mulgore, defeating the centaur warbands on the way.

After Hyjal, the Horde claimed the eastern Barrens as Durotar. The rest of the plains stayed neutral ground between Orgrimmar and Theramore for a time, until the Horde built its towns and watch towers there and made the Barrens the heart of its lands.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Barrens (Third War and aftermath, Cycle of Hatred, World of Warcraft)

entries.title: The Wandering Tribes
body: For countless generations the tauren roamed the Barrens, hunting kodo, thunder lizards, cheetah and zhevra, and seeking the wisdom of the Earth Mother. Their tent villages moved with the seasons and the weather. The wandering tribes were united only by their hatred of the centaurs, who hunted them for sport.

The tauren made the centaurs pay for every attack, but they had no love for war, and always chose to move on rather than throw their lives away. A year of peace was always followed by a year of war. They accepted the cycle as the only life they knew, until the orcs came.

entries.title: The Great Beasts of the Plains
body: The Barrens are still a land of great beasts: kodo herds and thunder lizards on the Field of Giants, zhevra and cheetah on the open plains, and the rare, legendary creatures the tauren hunt to prove themselves. A tauren who brings back the trophy of one of these beasts has earned a name among the hunters.
